# Authentication & Credential Management Operational Procedure

## Purpose

This procedure provides the step-by-step operational instructions that IAM Engineering follows to implement the identification, authentication, session management, and authenticator management requirements defined in the Example Org Authentication & Credential Management Standard. Executing this procedure ensures that only uniquely identified and authenticated users, devices, and processes gain access to Example Org systems, and that the resulting configurations and evidence are captured and retained.

## Scope

This procedure is performed by IAM Engineering on all Example Org authentication infrastructure, including the [Identity Provider], [Directory Service], [MDM Solution], [PKI], and all systems that enforce logon, session, and banner controls. It applies to privileged accounts, non-privileged accounts, non-organizational (external) users, and devices that connect to Example Org networks, and runs continuously as account, session, and authenticator events occur.

## Prerequisites

- Administrative access to the [Identity Provider], [Directory Service], [MDM Solution], [Endpoint Management Console], and [Web/Application Gateway]
- Access to the [Ticketing System] for change records and exception tracking
- Access to the [PKI] and [Certificate Authority] for public key-based authentication steps
- Access to the [Documentation Repository] for policy, plan, and evidence retention
- An approved [System Security and Privacy Plan] for each in-scope system, where the Standard requires plan-documented values
- Current CISA phishing-resistant authentication guidance and the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite

## Procedure Steps

### Enforce invalid logon attempt limits [NIST AC-7 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

1. Open the [Identity Provider] administration console and navigate to the authentication/lockout policy settings.
1. Set the maximum consecutive invalid logon attempts to `[Assignment: organization-defined number]` within a `[Assignment: organization-defined time period]`.
1. Set the enforced threshold to five (5) consecutive invalid attempts within a fifteen (15) minute window for all account types.
1. Apply the policy to all authentication endpoints and verify enforcement with a test account by exceeding the threshold and confirming the lockout triggers.
1. Export the resulting configuration and file it as part of the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Automate lockout response actions [NIST AC-7 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Identity Provider] lockout policy, configure the automated action taken when the maximum unsuccessful attempts are exceeded.
1. Select and configure at least one of: automatic lock for a minimum of thirty (30) minutes; lock until released by an administrator; delay the next logon prompt per `[Assignment: organization-defined delay algorithm]`; notify the system administrator; or `[Assignment: organization-defined action]`.
1. Configure administrator notification so that a lockout event generates an alert to the IAM Engineering on-call channel via the [Ticketing System].
1. Document the administrator release process: verify the requester's identity per the identity verification steps in this procedure, then unlock the account from the [Identity Provider] console.
1. Record the configured action in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Configure mobile device purge on unsuccessful logon attempts [NIST AC-7(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

1. Open the [MDM Solution] console and select the device compliance policy applied to `[Assignment: organization-defined mobile devices]`.
1. Configure the device wipe setting to purge or wipe information after ten (10) consecutive unsuccessful logon attempts.
1. Set the purge technique per `[Assignment: organization-defined purging or wiping requirements and techniques]` (e.g., full device wipe versus work-profile wipe).
1. Assign the policy to all enrolled mobile device groups and verify enforcement on a test device.
1. Capture the resulting policy in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Limit biometric logon attempts [NIST AC-7(3)]

1. In the [Identity Provider] or [Endpoint Management Console] biometric authentication settings, set the maximum consecutive unsuccessful biometric attempts to `[Assignment: organization-defined number]`.
1. Configure the fallback behavior on exhaustion (revert to the primary authenticator or lock per the lockout steps above).
1. Verify enforcement with a test enrollment and record the setting in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Allow alternative authentication factors after lockout [NIST AC-7(4)]

1. In the [Identity Provider], configure the post-lockout authentication path to permit `[Assignment: organization-defined authentication factors]` different from the primary factors once the consecutive invalid attempt threshold is exceeded.
1. Apply an independent limit of `[Assignment: organization-defined number]` consecutive invalid attempts through the alternative factors during a `[Assignment: organization-defined time period]`.
1. Test the full path: exceed the primary threshold, authenticate via the alternative factor, and confirm both limits are enforced independently.

### Display and enforce the system use notification [NIST AC-8 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

1. Compose the banner text in the [Identity Provider] logon configuration so it states that: system usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit; unauthorized use is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording.
1. Include the statements that users are accessing a U.S. Government system and accessing a system that contains U.S. Government information, consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and guidelines.
1. Configure the banner to display before access is granted and to remain on screen until the user acknowledges the usage conditions and takes an explicit action to log on or further access the system.
1. For publicly accessible systems, configure the notification to display under `[Assignment: organization-defined conditions]` before further access, include references to monitoring/recording/auditing only where consistent with privacy accommodations for such systems, and include a description of authorized uses of the system.
1. Confirm the displayed banner on each authentication portal, capture screenshots, and retain them with the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Limit concurrent sessions [NIST AC-10 High | ARC-AMPE AC-10 AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Identity Provider] session policy settings, set the concurrent session limit for each account/account type to one (1) session.
1. For any role requiring more than one concurrent session, confirm the requirement is expressly documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan before raising the limit for that account type.
1. Test with two simultaneous logins on a test account to confirm the earlier session is blocked or terminated as configured.
1. Retain the session configuration in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Enforce device lock on inactivity and unattended systems [NIST AC-11 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Endpoint Management Console] and [MDM Solution], configure automatic device lock after fifteen (15) minutes of inactivity for both remote and internal access connections.
1. Configure the lock screen to conceal previously visible information with a publicly viewable image, per `[Assignment: organization-defined image]`.
1. Publish the user requirement — via [Ticketing System] knowledge base article and onboarding material — that users must initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended.
1. Verify that the device lock releases only after the user reestablishes access using the established identification and authentication procedures (username/password plus MFA), and never without re-authentication.

### Define workstation use procedures for ePHI [HIPAA 164.310(b)]

1. Document, in the workstation use procedure maintained in the [Documentation Repository], the proper functions to be performed on workstations accessing electronic protected health information.
1. Specify in the same document the manner in which those functions are to be performed and the physical attributes of the surroundings of each workstation or workstation class that can access ePHI.
1. Disseminate the procedure to all staff with ePHI-accessing workstations and obtain acknowledgment through the [Ticketing System] workflow.
1. Update the document when workstation classes, locations, or functions change.

### Terminate sessions automatically and provide logout [NIST AC-12 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-12 AE Mandatory | NIST AC-12(1) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(1) AE Mandatory | NIST AC-12(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(2) AE Mandatory | NIST AC-12(3) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(3) AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iii) Addressable]

1. In the [Identity Provider] and [Web/Application Gateway] session policies, configure automatic session termination after `[Assignment: organization-defined conditions or trigger events]` occur.
1. Configure electronic session termination after a predetermined time of inactivity on all systems that maintain ePHI.
1. Enable a user-initiated logout capability on every information resource that uses authentication to gain access; for ARC-AMPE scope, confirm the resources are defined in the applicable security and privacy plans.
1. Configure an explicit logout message confirming termination of the authenticated session; use the standard message documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (e.g., "Your session has been terminated").
1. Configure an explicit warning message indicating the session will end in `[Assignment: organization-defined time]`, and confirm that the time-until-end value is specified in the applicable security and privacy plan.
1. Export the session policy configuration into the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Restrict ePHI system access to authorized persons and programs [HIPAA 164.312(a)(1)]

1. In the [Directory Service] and application access controls, configure access so only persons or software programs granted access rights per § 164.308(a)(4) can reach systems maintaining ePHI.
1. Reconcile the access list against approved access rights before enabling access, and verify with a negative test using an account outside the authorized list.

### Assign unique user identifiers [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(i) Required | NIST IA-2 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-2 | ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Directory Service], assign a unique name and/or number to every user for identifying and tracking identity; never reuse identifiers across users.
1. Uniquely identify and authenticate all organizational users and associate that unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users.
1. Employ identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines, requiring system/network authenticators and unique user identifiers for all organizational users.
1. Configure the [Service Desk] workflow so that any help desk transaction with information security and privacy implications requires verified user identification before action.
1. For non-organizational users, uniquely identify and authenticate them or the processes acting on their behalf, using identity proofing compliant with NIST SP 800-63 at IAL-2/AAL-2 and requiring unique user identifiers (see the non-organizational user steps below).

### Establish emergency access procedures for ePHI [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(ii) Required]

1. Document, in the [Documentation Repository], the procedure for obtaining necessary ePHI during an emergency (e.g., break-glass account activation, approver chain, and post-event review).
1. Implement the emergency access mechanism in the [Identity Provider] and test it as `[Assignment: organization-defined test frequency]` requires.
1. Log each emergency activation in the [Ticketing System] and review it after the event.

### Implement ePHI encryption and decryption [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv) Addressable]

1. Enable a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information at rest and in transit on all systems maintaining ePHI.
1. Verify the implementation uses the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards wherever the system contains PII.

### Manage the identification and authentication policy and procedures [NIST IA-1 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.316(b)(1) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(i) Required | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(ii) Required | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(iii) Required]

1. IAM Engineering develops, documents, and disseminates the identification and authentication policy (addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance) and the supporting procedures to `[Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]`.
1. The designated official `[Assignment: organization-defined official]` manages the development, documentation, and dissemination of the policy and procedures.
1. Review and update the policy and procedures at least every one (1) year and following `[Assignment: organization-defined events]`, including assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents, and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
1. Maintain all HIPAA Security Rule policies and procedures in written (electronic) form in the [Documentation Repository], with a written record of any required action, activity, or assessment.
1. Retain required documentation for 6 years from the date of creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later.
1. Make the documentation available in the [Documentation Repository] to all persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which it pertains.
1. Review the documentation periodically and update it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of ePHI.

### Implement multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts [NIST IA-2(1) Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-2(1) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(1) AE Mandatory | FedRAMP IA-2(2)]

1. In the [Identity Provider], enable an MFA enforcement policy on all privileged account roles and administrative consoles.
1. Select only phishing-resistant methods per current CISA guidance (e.g., FIDO2 security keys or PIV smart cards).
1. Enroll each privileged account holder, verify enrollment in the MFA admin console, and export the MFA enrolment report.
1. Confirm enforcement by attempting privileged access without the second factor and verifying denial.

### Implement multi-factor authentication for non-privileged accounts [NIST IA-2(2) Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-2(2) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(2) AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Identity Provider], enable MFA for all non-privileged, non-consumer account types.
1. For consumer accounts, where MFA is not mandated, promote voluntary enrollment and record the current enrollment rate from the MFA enrolment report.
1. Export the MFA enrolment report covering all non-privileged account types and retain it as process evidence.

### Individually authenticate users to shared accounts [NIST IA-2(5) High | ARC-AMPE IA-2(5) AE Mandatory]

1. Where shared accounts or authenticators are employed, configure the [Identity Provider] or [Privileged Access Solution] so each user is individually authenticated before access to the shared account or resource is granted.
1. Maintain the list of shared accounts and their authorized users in the [Documentation Repository].

### Require a separate device as an MFA factor [NIST IA-2(6) | FedRAMP IA-2(6) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(6) AE Mandatory]

1. For MFA to local, network, and remote access to both privileged and non-privileged accounts, configure the [Identity Provider] so one factor is provided by a device separate from the system gaining access.
1. Verify the separate device meets `[Assignment: organization-defined strength of mechanism requirements]`, and for ARC-AMPE scope that it implements the latest published FIPS 140-compliant cryptography.
1. Record the approved separate-device authenticator types in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Implement replay-resistant authentication [NIST IA-2(8) Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-2(8) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(8) AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Identity Provider] and [Web/Application Gateway], enable replay-resistant mechanisms (e.g., nonce or timestamp-based challenge/response, or protocol-level replay protection such as SAML/OIDC nonce validation) for access to privileged and non-privileged accounts.
1. Verify with a captured-traffic replay test that a replayed authentication is rejected.

### Provide single sign-on [NIST IA-2(10)]

1. Configure the [Identity Provider] to provide single sign-on for `[Assignment: organization-defined system accounts and services]`.
1. Register each in-scope service as a relying party and confirm session behavior matches the concurrent session and termination settings above.

### Accept and verify PIV-compliant credentials [NIST IA-2(12) Low/Moderate/High | NIST IA-8(1) Low/Moderate/High]

1. Configure the [Identity Provider] to accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials, including from other federal agencies.
1. Validate certificates against the [PKI] trust anchor and check revocation status before granting access.

### Implement out-of-band authentication [NIST IA-2(13)]

1. In the [Identity Provider], enable the out-of-band mechanisms `[Assignment: organization-defined out-of-band authentication]` under `[Assignment: organization-defined conditions]`.
1. Test the out-of-band flow end to end and record the configuration in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Verify the identity of persons seeking ePHI access [HIPAA 164.312(d)]

1. Implement, through the [Identity Provider] authentication flow and the [Service Desk] verification script, procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed.
1. Require the verification steps before initial account issuance, on any help desk transaction with security implications, and on credential re-issuance.

### Identify and authenticate devices before connection [NIST IA-3 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-3 AE Mandatory | NIST IA-3(1) | NIST IA-3(3) | NIST IA-3(4)]

1. Uniquely identify and authenticate `[Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices]` before establishing a `[Selection: local; remote; network]` connection.
1. For devices requiring authentication, use at minimum shared information (MAC or IP address) and access control lists to control remote network access; confirm the approved device types are defined in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.
1. Where cryptographically based bidirectional authentication is required for `[Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices]`, configure mutual certificate-based authentication (mTLS) via the [PKI] and verify both directions during a connection test.
1. Where addresses are allocated dynamically, standardize dynamic address allocation lease information and lease duration per `[Assignment: organization-defined lease information and lease duration]`, and audit lease information when assigned to a device in the [DHCP/DNS Service] logs.
1. Handle device identification and authentication based on attestation by `[Assignment: organization-defined configuration management process]`.

### Manage authenticators across their lifecycle [NIST IA-5 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory | NIST IA-5(5) | NIST IA-5(6) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(6) AE Mandatory | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

1. Verify the identity of the individual, group, role, service, or device receiving an authenticator as part of initial distribution, using the identity verification procedures in this document.
1. Establish initial authenticator content for any authenticators issued by the organization, ensuring sufficient strength of mechanism for the intended use and compliance with the most recent NIST Digital Identity Guidelines at IAL/AAL/FAL level 1 for Certification Class B, level 2 for Certification Class C, and level 3 for Certification Class D.
1. Implement administrative procedures — documented in the [Documentation Repository] and executed via the [Ticketing System] — for initial authenticator distribution, lost/compromised/damaged authenticators, and revocation.
1. Change all default authenticators (including vendor-supplied passwords) prior to first use, and immediately upon system installation.
1. Change or refresh authenticators per `[Assignment: organization-defined time period by authenticator type]` or when `[Assignment: organization-defined events]` occur; change or refresh authenticators immediately when they are known or suspected to be compromised.
1. For group or role accounts, change the authenticator whenever membership in those accounts changes; add this to the joiner/mover/leaver workflow in the [Ticketing System].
1. Protect authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification; require individuals to take, and have devices implement, specific controls `[Assignment: organization-defined authenticator protection controls]`; and protect authenticators commensurate with the security category of the information their use permits access to.
1. Require developers and installers of system components to provide unique authenticators or change default authenticators prior to delivery and installation; verify at acceptance before the component joins production.
1. Encrypt authentication assertions when passed through third parties such as a browser (e.g., SAML assertions encrypted using XML-Encryption, or OpenID Connect ID Tokens encrypted using JSON Web Encryption) — configure this in the [Identity Provider] federation settings.
1. Comply with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B for authenticator management; pair Organizational System/User Account passwords with MFA (strongly recommended for Organizational ACA Consumer Account passwords), and strongly recommend a policy requiring Organizational System/User Account passwords be changed or refreshed at least once every six (6) months.

### Enforce password policy and screening [NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Identity Provider] password policy settings, enforce password composition and complexity of `[Assignment: organization-defined composition and complexity rules]`, compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B: minimum eight (8) characters for ACA Consumer Accounts and all other accounts, and minimum twelve (12) characters for Administrator/Privileged Accounts; block dictionary words, allow passphrases, configure temporary passwords to trigger an immediate change to a permanent password, and apply `[Assignment: organization-defined mobile device complexity exception]` for mobile devices per organizational risk tolerance.
1. Maintain the list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords in the [Password Screening Service], update it per the frequency defined in the applicable security/privacy plans (not to exceed one (1) year), and update it immediately when organizational passwords are suspected to have been compromised directly or indirectly.
1. Configure the password change flow to verify at creation and update that new passwords do not appear on the compromised password list.
1. Configure all authentication endpoints to transmit passwords only over cryptographically protected channels (TLS) and disable any cleartext authentication protocols.
1. Store passwords using an approved salted key derivation function, preferably using a keyed hash; verify the storage configuration in the [Directory Service] and record the algorithm in the Authentication policy configuration export.
1. Require immediate selection of a new password upon completion of any account recovery, enforced in the [Identity Provider] recovery workflow.
1. Allow user selection of long passwords and passphrases, including spaces and all printable characters; set maximum length high enough to permit passphrases.
1. Deploy automated tools to assist users in selecting strong password authenticators (e.g., the password strength meter built into the [Identity Provider] enrollment page) and enable them on all password creation and change screens.

### Manage public key-based authentication [NIST IA-5(2) Moderate/High]

1. Enforce authorized access to the corresponding private key for all public key-based authentication (hardware-backed key storage or protected key store), and map the authenticated identity to the account of the individual or group in the [Identity Provider].
1. When PKI is used, validate certificates by constructing and verifying a certification path to an accepted trust anchor, including checking certificate status information (CRL/OCSP) via the [Certificate Authority].
1. Implement a local cache of revocation data to support path discovery and validation, and confirm the cache refreshes per `[Assignment: organization-defined revocation cache refresh]`.

### Manage the risk of multiple accounts per individual [NIST IA-5(8)]

1. Implement `[Assignment: organization-defined security controls]` to manage the risk of compromise due to individuals having accounts on multiple systems (e.g., SSO through the [Identity Provider] and consistent MFA enforcement).
1. Inventory multi-account holdings per user via the [Directory Service] and apply the controls to each account.

### Federate and bind credentials [NIST IA-5(9) | NIST IA-5(10) | NIST IA-5(15) | NIST IA-5(16)]

1. Use only the external organizations `[Assignment: organization-defined external organizations]` to federate credentials; configure each as a trusted identity provider in the [Identity Provider].
1. Bind identities and authenticators dynamically using the rules `[Assignment: organization-defined binding rules]`.
1. Use only General Services Administration-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management; verify product approval before procurement in the [Ticketing System].
1. Require issuance of `[Assignment: organization-defined types of and/or specific authenticators]` to be conducted `[Selection: in person; by a trusted external party]` before `[Assignment: organization-defined registration authority]` with authorization by `[Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]`.

### Manage biometric authenticators [NIST IA-5(12) | NIST IA-5(17) | NIST AC-7(3) linkage]

1. For biometric-based authentication, employ mechanisms that satisfy `[Assignment: organization-defined biometric quality requirements]`, verified at enrollment in the [Identity Provider] biometric enrollment flow.
1. Enable presentation attack detection mechanisms in the biometric authentication path and validate them with spoof-attempt testing before go-live.

### Restrict cached authenticators [NIST IA-5(13)]

1. In the [Endpoint Management Console] and [Identity Provider], prohibit the use of cached authenticators after `[Assignment: organization-defined time period]`.
1. Verify on a test endpoint that cached credentials expire at the configured limit and full re-authentication is required.

### Manage PKI trust stores [NIST IA-5(14)]

1. Establish and apply an organization-wide methodology for managing the content of PKI trust stores installed across all platforms — networks, operating systems, browsers, and applications — executed through the [Endpoint Management Console].
1. Baseline the approved trust store content, distribute it, and audit deviations.

### Deploy password managers [NIST IA-5(18)]

1. Employ `[Assignment: organization-defined password managers]` to generate and manage passwords, and protect the stored passwords using `[Assignment: organization-defined controls]`.
1. Distribute the password manager via the [Endpoint Management Console] and disable any policy requiring memorized rotation where the manager is in use.

### Obscure authentication feedback [NIST IA-6 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-6 AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Identity Provider] logon pages and all application authentication prompts, verify that authentication feedback (typed passwords, secret answers, one-time codes) is obscured and not echoed in cleartext.
1. Review each authentication surface and file confirmation in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Authenticate to cryptographic modules [NIST IA-7 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-7 AE Mandatory]

1. Implement mechanisms for authentication to each cryptographic module that meet the requirements of applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidelines.
1. Verify all systems containing PII use the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards, and record module modes of operation in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### Authenticate external organizations' credentials [NIST IA-8 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory | NIST IA-8(2) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-8(2) AE Mandatory | NIST IA-8(4) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-8(4) AE Mandatory | NIST IA-8(5) | NIST IA-8(6)]

1. Uniquely identify and authenticate non-organizational users, or processes acting on their behalf, using identity proofing and authentication compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 at IAL-2/AAL-2, with system/network authenticators and unique user identifiers.
1. Accept only external authenticators that are NIST-compliant; document and maintain the list of accepted external authenticators in the [Documentation Repository], reviewing it whenever a federation partner is added or removed.
1. Verify each external credential is certified as compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 document suite by an approved accreditation authority and meets or exceeds those guidelines; use General Services Administration-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management.
1. Conform to `[Assignment: organization-defined identity management profiles]` for identity management, defined using NIST SP 800-63-compliant identity proofing and authentication processes.
1. Accept and verify federated or PKI credentials that meet `[Assignment: organization-defined policy]` before mapping them to local accounts in the [Identity Provider].
1. Implement `[Assignment: organization-defined measures]` to disassociate user attributes or identifier assertion relationships among individuals, credential service providers, and relying parties.

### Require re-authentication on defined events [NIST IA-11 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-11 AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Identity Provider], configure forced re-authentication when `[Assignment: organization-defined circumstances or situations]` occur, including when authenticators, credentials, or roles change; when security categories of systems change; when execution of privileged functions occurs; and after a fixed time period of `[Assignment: organization-defined re-authentication period]`.
1. For ARC-AMPE scope, confirm each circumstance is defined in the applicable security and privacy plan before enabling the trigger.
1. Test each trigger (e.g., perform a privileged function and confirm the session requires re-authentication) and retain test results with the Authentication policy configuration export.

## Roles & Responsibilities

IAM Engineering is authorized and accountable to perform all steps in this procedure end to end, including configuration, verification, evidence capture (MFA enrolment report and Authentication policy configuration export), and handoffs to participant teams such as the [Service Desk] and [Endpoint Management] staff. Exceptions to any step must be requested through the [Ticketing System] and are reviewed and approved by `[Assignment: organization-defined official]` in coordination with IAM Engineering before they take effect.

## Related Standard

Example Org Authentication & Credential Management Standard
